description: Forward discounted-cash-flow valuation (two-stage Gordon-growth model) under YOUR assumptions: you give stage-1 growth, WACC, terminal growth and horizon; it returns the per-share intrinsic value (`value_per_share_cents`, cents of `result.reporting_currency`, never converted) and a 5×5 WACC × terminal-growth sensitivity grid. Valuein publishes no precomputed DCF, DDM or fair value: this tool is the only intrinsic value, and it is a scenario under the stated assumptions: a different discount rate is a different answer, so where it matters run more than one set of assumptions and give the range. In prose quote `result.metrics_display` verbatim (e.g. "$249.17"; each grid cell carries `value_per_share_display`), never the cents, and state the assumptions beside it. Inputs pulled from the filings (any can be overridden): FCF base = operating_cash_flow − capex; net_debt = total_debt − (cash + short-term investments), with `result.net_debt_basis` saying whether it was reported or assumed; shares = CommonSharesOutstanding, else net_income / eps_diluted (`result.shares_source`). Use the returned net debt, shares and bridge; never recompute them. `result.inputs_echo` and `result.inputs_provenance` cite each input's `fact_id` (the FCF base carries a `derived_id`). When every input came from cited facts (fcf_source "trend", no override) `result.outputs_provenance.value_per_share.derived_id` and each grid cell's `derived_id` encode your assumptions so the arithmetic can be re-derived: cite them beside the figure. An override, a three_statement run or a degenerate model ships no id: quote those as your own assumptions. A null `value_per_share_cents` (WACC ≤ terminal growth, FCF base ≤ 0, or a missing input) is NOT a zero valuation; `reason` explains. Optional `share_price` (a price the user gave, with its date) adds `result.upside_pct`. `fcf_source: "three_statement"` feeds the linked projection of `project_three_statement` into the same PV math (`stage1_growth_rate` then ignored; detail in `three_statement_detail`). Persists nothing: use `create_report` (report_type 'reverse_dcf') to save. Plan: Benchmark and above.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD) for the auto-pulled inputs. Fundamentals are filtered by SEC accepted_at (strict PIT). Omit to use the latest knowable inputs.

fcf_base_override.description: Override the auto-pulled FCF base (USD). Leave unset to use R2-derived.

fcf_source.description: "trend" (default): compound fcf_base by stage1_growth_rate every year (unchanged original behavior). "three_statement": derive the FCF stream from a full linked 3-statement projection instead — see the tool description for details.

share_price.description: Optional share price YOU supply (never from memory) for the company valued, same fields as a `compute_price_multiples` row (cik optional, ticker not used). Adds `result.upside_pct`: the DCF value per share against your price, with the price and its date in the figure's `derived_id`. Call it your price, user-supplied, with its date.

adjusted_through.description: For split_adjusted: the date the adjustment runs to (YYYY-MM-DD).

adjustment.description: How the close was adjusted; default raw. split_adjusted needs adjusted_through. total_return is refused for multiples.

as_of.description: When the price was observed, ISO 8601 with offset. Default: 16:00 America/New_York on price_date.

cik.description: SEC Central Index Key of the company. Preferred over a ticker.

close.description: Closing price per share, in `currency`: above 0, at most 10,000,000, at most 8 decimal places.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of the close, e.g. USD.

fx_rate.description: Units of the company's reporting currency per 1 unit of `currency`; needed when the currencies differ. Also yours.

price_date.description: Date the close belongs to, YYYY-MM-DD. Required: a price without a date is refused.

source_label.description: Your own note on where the price came from, at most 64 characters. Shown as yours.

shares_override.description: Override shares outstanding. Leave unset to use R2-derived.

stage1_years.description: Number of explicit high-growth projection years before the terminal stage (3–15). Defaults to 5.

three_statement_assumptions.description: Only used when fcf_source is "three_statement". Overrides for the underlying projection; unset fields use project_three_statement's defaults.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol of the company to value, e.g. AAPL, MSFT, BRK.B.

name: compute_dcf

_meta.description: Response metadata (provenance, point-in-time flag, freshness, request id and warnings). Every field is documented once in the agent contract (agent_contract.meta in the server's manifest.json).
